title: Preliminary pointed finite-over-smooth chart over an affine open base
statement: Let $p:Z\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $z\in Z$, put $s=p(z)$, and set $n=\dim_z(Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s))$ [def-kun-dimension, def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field]. There exist an affine open neighbourhood $j:S_0\hookrightarrow S$ of $s$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], an affine scheme $Y_0$, a scheme $W_0$, morphisms $b_0:W_0\to Z$, $\pi_0:W_0\to Y_0$, $h_0:Y_0\to S_0$, and points $w_0\in W_0$, $y_0\in Y_0$, $s_0\in S_0$ with $b_0(w_0)=z$, $\pi_0(w_0)=y_0$, $h_0(y_0)=s_0$, $j(s_0)=s$, and $pb_0=jh_0\pi_0$. The morphism $b_0$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and its induced map $\kappa(z)\to\kappa(w_0)$ is an isomorphism. The morphism $\pi_0$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $\pi_0^{-1}(\{y_0\})=\{w_0\}$. The morphism $h_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The induced extension $\kappa(y_0)/\kappa(s_0)$ is isomorphic over $\kappa(s_0)$ to $\kappa(s_0)(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ for some finite $r\geq0$, with algebraically independent variables.

source.place: Tag 052E, lemma-local-structure-finite-type, proof; Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof through the affine choice of Y and finite presentation of h.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $S_a\subseteq S$ containing $s$ and an affine open $Z_a\subseteq p^{-1}(S_a)$ containing $z$, using the affine-open basis. Write $p_a:Z_a\to S_a$ for the restriction. Every affine subpair for $p_a$ is an affine subpair for $p$, with the same map on sections, so [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] implies that $p_a$ is locally of finite type. Since both schemes are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) give quasi-compactness. Thus $p_a$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Open immersions identify the local rings and residue fields at retained points. Consequently the fibre $(Z_a)_s$ is the open part of $Z_s$ over $Z_a$, by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] applied with the same residue-field spectrum on both sides. Its dimension at $z$ is $n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace].

source.place: Tag 052E, lemma-local-structure-finite-type, proof: reduction to affine X and S; Tags 01IT, 01T2, 01SH, 01S7 and 01JR for the restriction details.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-refined-quasi-finite-polynomial-pure-transcendental] to the finite type affine morphism $p_a$ at $z$. It gives affine open neighbourhoods $S_0\subseteq S_a$ and $Z_0\subseteq p_a^{-1}(S_0)$ of $s,z$, and an $S_0$-map $q:Z_0\to A=\mathbf A^n_{S_0}$ that is of finite type with finite discrete fibres. Write $t=q(z)$ and $a:A\to S_0$ for projection. Then $\kappa(t)\cong\kappa(s)(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ over $\kappa(s)$ for some finite $0\le r\le n$. Let $j:S_0\hookrightarrow S$ and $i:Z_0\hookrightarrow Z$ be the composite open inclusions. The map $aq$ is the restricted structure map, so $pi=jaq$. In particular $j(s_0)=s$ for the point $s_0$ corresponding to $s$.

source.place: Tag 052E, lemma-local-structure-finite-type, first proof paragraph; Algebra Tag 0520, lemma-refined-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra.

proof.text: The point $z$ is isolated in the fibre of $q$ at $t$, since that fibre is discrete. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-at-point-elementary] to $q,z,t$; its local-finite-type hypothesis follows from the finite-type conclusion in step 2. Obtain an etale map $e:\widetilde Y\to A$, a point $y\in\widetilde Y$ with $e(y)=t$ and induced isomorphism $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(y)$, and an open $V\subseteq P=Z_0\times_A\widetilde Y$. Its projection $\rho:V\to\widetilde Y$ is finite, its fibre over $y$ has exactly one point $w$, and projection $V\to Z_0$ sends $w$ to $z$ with induced residue isomorphism $\kappa(z)\to\kappa(w)$.

source.place: Tag 052E, lemma-local-structure-finite-type, second proof paragraph: application of Tag 02LK, lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-at-point, clauses (a),(b),(i)--(iii).

proof.text: Choose an affine open $k:Y_0\hookrightarrow\widetilde Y$ containing $y$, and put $W_0=\rho^{-1}(Y_0)$, with projection $\pi_0:W_0\to Y_0$. The universal property identifies $W_0$ with $V\times_{\widetilde Y}Y_0$: a map into either is precisely a map to $V$ whose composite with $\rho$ factors through $Y_0$. Thus $\pi_0$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). Since $y$ belongs to $Y_0$, its inverse image remains exactly $\{w\}$; write the retained points as $w_0,y_0$. The restricted structure sheaves have the same stalks, so $\kappa(y_0)=\kappa(y)$ and $\kappa(w_0)=\kappa(w)$. The map $e_0=ek$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The open-fibre-product lemma identifies $P_0=Z_0\times_A Y_0$ with the open part of $P$ lying over $Y_0$; hence $W_0=V\cap P_0$ is open in $P_0$. Projection $P_0\to Z_0$ is etale as the base change of $e_0$. The inclusions $W_0\hookrightarrow P_0$ and $i:Z_0\hookrightarrow Z$ are open immersions, so their composite with this projection is an etale map $b_0:W_0\to Z$. It sends $w_0$ to $z$, and its residue map is the isomorphism of step 3 under the open-restriction identifications.

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof: replace Y by an affine neighbourhood and X prime by its inverse image; Tags 01JR, 01WL, 02GO, 02GN and 02GP for permanence.

proof.text: Set $h_0=ae_0:Y_0\to S_0$. The projection $a:\mathbf A^n_{S_0}\to S_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Since $e_0$ is etale, it is smooth of relative dimension $0$ in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]; hence [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2), with $m=0$, shows that $h_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $0+n=n$. Smoothness includes local finite presentation by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Both $Y_0$ and $S_0$ are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes $h_0$ affine and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) makes it quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Together these are precisely finite presentation as defined in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 052E, lemma-local-structure-finite-type, proof of clause (1); Tag 057K, proof through finite presentation of h; Tags 02NL and 01S7.

proof.text: The defining square of $P_0$ gives $q\operatorname{pr}_1=e_0\operatorname{pr}_2$. Restricting to $W_0$ and using step 2 yields $pb_0=jae_0\pi_0=jh_0\pi_0$. The chosen points satisfy $b_0(w_0)=z$, $\pi_0(w_0)=y_0$, $h_0(y_0)=s_0$ and $j(s_0)=s$. On residue fields, the map induced by $h_0$ is the composite $\kappa(s_0)\to\kappa(t)\to\kappa(y_0)$. The second arrow is the isomorphism supplied by step 3 and unchanged in step 4; the first is the rational-function extension supplied by step 2, with $\kappa(s_0)=\kappa(s)$ under the open inclusion $j$. Therefore $\kappa(y_0)\cong\kappa(s_0)(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ over $\kappa(s_0)$. All remaining asserted properties were established in steps 4 and 5.
